title: Choose a service
note: Embedded shop-branded booking, also usable as a standalone page. Known service and diagnosis entry both lead into the same job journey.

title: Describe the bike & problem
note: Service questions appear here, not in a separate survey. Media is optional. Upload selection stays local in this review artefact.

title: Choose drop-off or appointment
note: Proposed date in this fixed scenario is 17 September. The production calendar must recompute availability atomically. Drop-off never implies a promised start.

title: Contact & update preferences
note: No customer account. Matching a phone number never exposes existing records. Marketing permission is separate from job updates. The review artefact uses fictional details.

title: Request received
note: Review-mode request is not confirmed. Automatic acceptance is a separate configured path, shown by the confirmed screen after successful capacity reservation.

title: Review incoming requests
note: Staff can distinguish requests from confirmed capacity and review the customer’s own words. Operational counts stay in scope; this is not a report.

title: Confirm the request
note: Accept reserves capacity once. Reject includes a human explanation. A failed acceptance must leave the request unchanged.

title: Booking confirmed
note: This is the result for reviewed acceptance or a successful automatically accepted booking. It must never appear before reservation succeeds.

title: The workshop at a glance
note: Queues and custody are independent of work state. Counters are operational, not a reporting dashboard. A walk-in uses the same job model.

title: Book the bike into the shop
note: Explicit custody event. Default auto-print can be set by the shop. Recording arrival must succeed even if the printer is offline, with a visible print task.

title: Print & attach the bike tag
note: Valid specimen QR encodes https://wheelhouse.example/staff/jobs/WH-1042 (reserved example domain). Final label size, driver, customer-detail policy and 1D barcode need physical shop validation. “Acknowledged” is a designed state, not evidence of a real print.

title: Scan → authenticated job
note: Staff-only QR route. A signed-out scan returns to this job after login. A different shop gets no customer or job disclosure. The local artefact does not access a camera.

title: Open the mechanic’s job
note: Phone is a working tool for inspection, not a shrunk desktop table. Opening a job does not claim it or start work.

title: Inspect & explain the findings
note: Completed template answers are preserved if the shop later changes the checklist. Media is explicitly attached to the job and shared with the customer when sent.

title: Build the itemised quote
note: £65 + £28 + £18 + £12 = £123 proposed. Parts and fitting are explained as one repair dependency; declining necessary fitting must not authorise an unsafe partial repair.

title: Send the approval request
note: Send honours selected channels at send time; no blind retries after uncertain delivery. This artefact routes to the customer preview and sends nothing.

title: Approve each line
note: Interactive selections update the total. Both brake lines remain individually visible and their dependency is explicit. Consent is bound to quote revision 2. Unchecked new lines are declined.

title: Know what was agreed
note: Confirmation reflects selections from the interactive quote screen. The standard walkthrough uses £111 with the £12 cable declined.

title: Shop sees the exact agreement
note: Fixed canonical £111 scenario. Any additional effort must reserve capacity, independently of monetary consent. Approval does not mean the work is already scheduled.

title: Allocate work in the diary
note: Proposed allocation shown for review. Move saves atomically and retains the old allocation on conflict. Shared-to-mechanic transfer must not double-count. Day, week and month views share one capacity model.

title: Take work from the shared queue
note: Alternative to desk allocation: shared-queue claim is atomic. If another mechanic takes it first, show the owner and leave capacity unchanged.

title: Do the approved work
note: Only approved work is actionable. Work finished, ready for collection and physically collected are separate events. Notes are staff-only unless explicitly shared.

title: Handle a parts delay
note: Exception scenario: revised date and remaining effort are independent. This branch does not silently overwrite the canonical on-time walkthrough.

title: One job conversation
note: Illustrative sent/received states. Production inbound matching, consent and provider capability must be proven; sending in this artefact is navigation only.

title: Customer follows up
note: Secure customer thread. The ready-state fixture illustrates a conversation; delay messages use the same composition. Do not show staff-only notes or unrelated customer history.

title: Handoff agreed work to Lightspeed
note: R-Series is provisional. These are target UI states, not proof of API access. Customer association is for this job only. Actual work-order, stock and employee permissions gate implementation.

title: See the linked work order
note: External link/deep-link availability is an API proof item; reference lookup remains a safe designed fallback. No Wheelhouse payment, refund or invoice controls.

title: Finish, check, then mark ready
note: A distinct final check separates work finished from ready for collection. Message delivery failure cannot undo work completion or falsely mark delivery successful.

title: Customer is invited to collect
note: Readiness is not collection or settlement. Show a concise handover and opening hours; no online payment CTA.

title: Record physical collection
note: Custody leaves “In shop” only after explicit confirmation. Staff use the existing till process independently. No payment gate or settlement status is invented.

title: Collected, with a durable history
note: Locked collected record. Reopening needs permission and a reason; it must not erase the original collection or imply the bike is physically back.

title: “I don’t know what’s wrong”
note: Alternative fixture: Oliver’s unknown problem. The production journey retains these entered details; atlas navigation returns to the canonical Maya fixture after this branch. No diagnostic price is invented.

title: Triage an unknown problem
note: £25/30 min are illustrative shop choices, not an approved fee policy. Customer must see and agree the assessment before it becomes chargeable. Approval uses the same component as the service quote.

title: Book an exact appointment
note: Fixed timed-appointment specimen; chosen mode must be carried through request and confirmation in production. This branch routes back to canonical drop-off contact details in the atlas.

title: Explain unavailable dates
note: Server is authoritative at submit. No false success, no silent overbooking, and no customer waiting-list feature added.

title: Change or cancel a booking
note: Requesting a change does not discard the original booking. Capacity is exchanged atomically on acceptance. In-shop cancellation needs staff handling.

title: Date change is pending
note: The old hold remains while a new-date request awaits a decision. Acceptance and rejection reuse the request review decision pattern.

title: Confirm a cancellation
note: Explicit confirmation before releasing the reservation. This screen applies before bike arrival; no refund flow is introduced.

title: Cancellation acknowledged
note: Cancellation is distinct from rejected and expired requests. Keep the cancellation event in staff history.

title: Decline with an explanation
note: Staff-written explanation is required in the proposed UX. Confirm the shop’s rejection wording during review.

title: Customer sees a declined request
note: Clear customer outcome. No booked status or live hold remains after rejection.

title: Expired request / private link
note: Reservation expiry and secure-link expiry are different backend events. The lower section is the shared safe-access explanation; production uses the appropriate specific heading, without disclosing another customer’s data.

title: A quote changed before approval
note: Stale submission never silently approves new prices. Only changed lines need new approval; unchanged decisions stay intact.

title: Agree a spending ceiling
note: Alternative approval policy to validate with Jack. This is a fixed £120 specimen, not live permission storage. A changed limit requires matching consent wording; exceeding the limit or scope requires a new decision.

title: Return to the private progress link
note: Canonical in-progress snapshot. Production progress derives from the current job state; the atlas intentionally shows named state specimens rather than a full simulation.

title: A diary move cannot be saved
note: Same conflict pattern covers stale job edits, with current actor/version shown and edits preserved for comparison rather than silent overwrite.

title: Another mechanic claimed it
note: Atomic claim. A concurrency conflict is an ordinary usable state, not an unexplained error toast.

title: Uncertain Lightspeed handoff
note: Unknown is different from failed. Reconciliation must verify job/customer/amount; it cannot blindly attach an arbitrary ID. Retry only after duplicate absence is established.

title: Printer offline / output unknown
note: Durable scoped print tasks survive restart. Unknown acknowledgement never claims physical success. Native Mac printer-host support is not assumed.

title: Deliberately reprint a tag
note: Reprint is an intentional new task with actor/reason, not automatic replay of an unknown task.

title: A message needs attention
note: Three distinct delivery states: queued, confirmed failed, unknown. Provider responses must drive labels; mock delivery is not integration proof.

title: Sign in after scanning
note: Visual sign-in reference only; final auth method follows the existing authentication implementation. No credentials leave this file. Revoked accounts cannot regain old-session access after reactivation.

title: Wrong shop or revoked access
note: No bike, customer, price or job-existence details from another tenant. Server enforces the boundary; hiding a button is insufficient.

title: Reopen without rewriting history
note: Proposed manager-permission boundary to validate. A checked return must create a separate custody event; the unchecked default keeps custody out of shop.

title: Find parts, SKUs & labour
note: Grouped product variants with distinct SKU/barcode identity. Catalogue price is copied into the proposal; approval snapshots remain immutable.

title: Create a walk-in job
note: Staff-only customer search. Walk-in with bike present shares the explicit custody/checklist event and capacity checks.

title: The complete job workspace
note: Job is independent of a sale. Product, customer, bike and service writer controls belong here; separate work status and custody are visible.

title: Audit changes to the job
note: Actor, time and prior decisions remain attributable. This is job activity, not a reporting suite.

title: Full paper job card
note: Tag and A4 card share a stable QR but different layouts. Physical printer and stock need verification. No invoice/receipt template.

title: Week view of workshop capacity
note: Week overview counts shared work once. Leave reduces available minutes. This is live operational capacity, not group/report analytics.

title: Month view and closed days
note: September 2026 starts Tuesday; Sundays are closed. Illustrative utilisation is for this shop only. Clicking a day in this fixed atlas opens the Thursday diary specimen.

title: Shop identity & booking appearance
note: Uses existing shop theming direction. Appearance controls affect the embed and customer portal; staff brand stays consistent. No group or subscription controls.

title: Service catalogue & questions
note: Extend existing service model rather than add a parallel catalogue. Durations feed capacity; prices feed quotes; bookability feeds the customer embed.

title: Configure a service
note: Shown order is part of the template. New template version affects future jobs only. Example brake question should be conditional to the customer concern in production.

title: Hours, leave & available effort
note: Shop opening hours and mechanic effort are distinct. Leave, closures and breaks reduce available capacity; the public calendar must not expose staff leave details.

title: Set booking & diary behaviour
note: Four-hour expiry and 60-minute staff reserve are proposed review defaults, not previously agreed policy. Per-service overrides remain explicit. Embed can preselect/filter a service; no separate website builder.

title: Connect email, SMS & WhatsApp
note: No provider is claimed connected. Shop-owned credentials and actual send/inbound capability are P00 proof tasks for all three channels.

title: Configure a messaging channel
note: Provider-specific form and inbound identifiers depend on chosen provider; exact fields shown are a design assumption. Secrets are not collected or sent by this artefact.

title: Verify delivery before enabling
note: Setup remains unavailable for live sending until proof. This screen does not manufacture a successful test or enable fake provider credentials.

title: Edit a customer message template
note: Template controls belong to messaging, not duplicate generic settings. Provider limits and WhatsApp approved templates must constrain the final editor.

title: Connect the one chosen Lightspeed
note: One adapter only. R-Series is provisional pending first-shop selection. This artefact does not perform OAuth or assert full API access. The real Connect button will start provider authorisation once P00a passes.

title: Verify connector capabilities
note: Readiness brief LS-01–09 remains the actual evidence gate. This is an honest unconnected setup state alongside designed connected job states.

title: Register printers & scan a fixture
note: Windows agent is existing implementation direction. Final label dimensions are deliberately not fabricated; scanner and paper proof remains pending.

title: Manage staff access
note: Role labels are proposed presentation of existing permission boundaries, not new group-level roles. Deactivation must permanently revoke old sessions.

title: Change or deactivate access
note: Deactivation gets a confirmation screen. Actor history remains even when staff access is removed.

title: Confirm staff deactivation
note: Mutation is simulated only. Production invalidates tokens at the server and scopes the staff member to the current shop.

title: Customer & bike records
note: Normal record maintenance remains in scope. No bulk customer import, backfill or public phone-history lookup.

title: Edit a customer and bike
note: Staff can add/edit bikes without mandatory serial numbers. Access and history are shop scoped. Editing contacts does not retroactively change approval snapshots.

title: Review a possible duplicate
note: Explicit staff review with surviving values. Production must block cross-shop merge and retain attribution; there is no automatic name/phone merge.

title: Change customer update channels
note: Preferences must be checked at send time; changing them cancels incompatible queued reminders. The secure link remains usable regardless of channel selection.

title: A clear save confirmation
note: Shared acknowledgement specimen. Production stays on the edited page with a specific inline confirmation (e.g. “Service saved”) and current values, rather than sending every edit here.

title: Work finished; prepare the handover
note: Work-finished is an explicit state before readiness. The walkthrough visits the POS handoff next; the shop may link it earlier. Collection and payment remain separate.

title: Mechanic’s job conversation
note: A staff phone opens the staff conversation, never the customer’s private link. Staff-only notes are separate from outgoing messages.

title: Booking service temporarily unavailable
note: Retained P10 service/error visibility. Never infer booking failure after an ambiguous submission: that separate case needs request-status lookup before retrying. No disaster-recovery feature or guarantee.
